justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 and general brief requirements via the Catalogue Service (with Catalogue Manager and Repository Component), Circulation Service (Borrowing Engine), and Web Frontend (Catalog and Circulation Components supporting patron self-service and librarian operations).
justifications.performance_efficiency: R-05 is explicitly targeted through a dedicated Elasticsearch container with an in-memory Query Caching Layer, asynchronous event publishing via RabbitMQ and Outbox components, and client-side caching using TanStack Query in the Catalog Component.
justifications.compatibility: Explicit adapters and protocols interface cleanly with all external systems: IdP via OAuth2/OIDC in the Authentication & Authorization Filter, Payment Gateway via TLS 1.3 in Circulation Service, and Notification Provider via Provider Integration Client over REST.
justifications.usability: Both Library Patron and Librarian actors are accommodated through the Web Frontend SPA via dedicated Catalog and Circulation components for self-service and staff workflows, though role-tailored interface segregation could be detailed further.
justifications.reliability: High reliability is ensured via Resilience & Circuit Breaker Filters, CloudNativePG automated failover in PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ Quorum Queues with Raft consensus, dead-letter exchanges (DLX), and transactional Outbox Pattern components across services.
justifications.security: Enforces EU data residency across PostgreSQL Storage Subspace and RabbitMQ volumes. Robust controls include mTLS, propagated JWTs, OAuth2/OIDC authentication, AES-256/TDE encryption at rest, SCRAM-SHA-256, HashiCorp Vault secret storage, and pgaudit compliance logging.
justifications.maintainability: Highly maintainable through a modular microservice decomposition (Catalogue, Circulation, Notification Services) with well-separated domain managers, controllers, DAOs, and asynchronous decoupling over RabbitMQ event messaging.
justifications.portability: Containers and components rely on standard technologies (Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL StatefulSets via CloudNativePG, RabbitMQ) that can run in any standard containerized cloud or on-premise infrastructure adhering to EU residency.

PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch cluster with query caching, TanStack Query client caching, and Spring Cloud Gateway dispatching directly address sub-800ms search latency under peak load.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cache hit ratio under high concurrency
tradeoffs: In-memory query caching trades memory consumption for sub-second read performance

PERF-02.justification: Transactional writes go to PostgreSQL while indexing is decoupled via the transactional outbox pattern, RabbitMQ, and asynchronous consumer listeners, ensuring sub-5-minute index propagation without impacting search latency.
sensitivity_points: RabbitMQ message consumption rate and queue depth under peak write load
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of search index traded for decoupled high-throughput write processing

AVAIL-01.justification: Elasticsearch clustering handles index node failures. Circulation workflows rely strictly on PostgreSQL, completely isolating loan transactions from search node outages.
tradeoffs: Replica overhead across nodes trades infrastructure cost for continuous query availability

AVAIL-02.justification: The Web Frontend is a stateless React SPA behind Nginx. Redundant frontend instances and gateway health-checking provide seamless traffic failover without session or loan data loss.
sensitivity_points: Load balancer health check intervals for detecting dead SPA/Nginx instances
tradeoffs: Stateless SPA design trades initial bundle download size for effortless horizontal failover

MOD-01.justification: The Catalogue Service lacks an explicit abstraction or pluggable provider adapter layer for external digital content providers, requiring core service and domain logic modifications.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between Catalogue Manager and specific item ingestion schemas
tradeoffs: Simpler initial domain model trades extensibility for lower initial design complexity

MOD-02.justification: The Borrowing Engine utilizes the Specification Pattern in Java code rather than an external configuration-driven rule engine, likely requiring code redeployment to modify business rules.
sensitivity_points: Hard-coded loan rule specifications compiled into Java binaries
tradeoffs: Compile-time code safety in specifications trades off runtime rule configurability

SEC-01.justification: Data residency is enforced across the stack with EU-bound persistent volumes in RabbitMQ, localized Redis EU clusters, and EU-constrained PostgreSQL storage subspaces.
sensitivity_points: Infrastructure region binding configurations across all data stores
tradeoffs: Restricting deployment to EU regions trades global edge replication for regulatory compliance

SEC-02.justification: API Gateway filters tokens and permissions, and PostgreSQL includes pgaudit for logging. Explicit object-level authorization (ABAC) in the Circulation Service could be more thoroughly defined.
sensitivity_points: Validation of resource ownership against JWT subject claims
Completeness of pgaudit capture for unauthorized attempts
tradeoffs: Deep inspection of patron ownership and audit logging trades small latency for security
